identity.title: Exploring molecular complexity with ALMA (EMoCA): Simulations of branched carbon-chain chemistry in Sgr B2(N)

paper_type_evidence.quote: The simulations presented here make use of the coupled gas-phase, grain-surface, and ice-mantle chemical kinetics model *MAGICKAL*, adopting a set of physical conditions deemed appropriate specifically to the Galactic Center hot-core source Sgr B2(N2).

question.value: Explain the observed i:n ratio of propyl cyanide in Sgr B2(N2), predict abundances of the four butyl cyanide isomers and alkanes up to pentane, and test for n-butyl cyanide in EMoCA data

evidence.quote: Through computational methods, we seek to explain the observed $i$:$n$ ratio for propyl cyanide, and to predict the abundances of the four different forms of the homologous nitrile, butyl cyanide (C$_4$H$_9$CN).
This paper makes use of the following ALMA data: ADS/JAO.ALMA#2011.0.00017.S, ADS/JAO.ALMA#2012.1.00012.S.
This paper makes use of the following ALMA data: ADS/JAO.ALMA#2011.0.00017.S, ADS/JAO.ALMA#2012.1.00012.S.

what.value: Gas-phase rate data for CN addition to C3H6 and C4H8 at 195 K and 298 K

evidence.loc: 2.2.2 CN addition to carbon multiple bonds
evidence.quote: based on the rates provided by Gannon et al. (2007) at 195 K and 298 K

what.value: Observed i/n propyl cyanide ratio 0.40 ± 0.06 and abundances toward Sgr B2(N2)

evidence.quote: indicating an $i$/$n$ ratio of $0.40 \pm 0.06$

what.value: Spectroscopic predictions for n-C4H9CN in CDMS

evidence.quote: Using the spectroscopic predictions of (cite: Ordu12) that are available in the CDMS catalog, we searched for *n-*C$_4$H$_9$CN

what.value: Basic chemical and physical treatments of MAGICKAL

evidence.quote: The basic chemical and physical treatments used in the model have been described in detail in past publications; in particular, by (cite: GWWH) and (cite: Garrod13).

what.value: Chemical network based on Belloche et al. 2014 with Mueller16 additions; initial elemental abundances as Garrod13

evidence.quote: The chemical network is based on that presented by (cite: Belloche14), and includes the recent additions by (cite: Mueller16).

analysis_steps.goal: Run collapse and warm-up chemical models

method.value: MAGICKAL three-phase rate-equation model with free-fall collapse then warm-up from 8 to 400 K at three timescales

evidence.quote: The physical model consists of two stages: free-fall collapse, followed by a dynamically-static warm-up.

key_parameters.value: n_H = 2e8 cm-3 post-collapse; zeta = 1.3e-17 s-1; 0.1 micron grains

evidence.quote: A post-collapse gas density of $n_{\mathrm{H}} = 2 \times 10^{8}$ cm$^{-3}$ is assumed
A canonical cosmic-ray ionization rate of $\zeta$ = $1.3 \times 10^{-17}$ s$^{-1}$ is assumed

validation.value: Compared model ice abundances and i:n ratio with observations; tested high CN-addition barriers

evidence.quote: In order to test the dependence of the model results on these barriers, we re-ran the collapse model and the three subsequent warm-up models

analysis_steps.goal: Search for n-C4H9CN in EMoCA spectrum and derive upper limit

method.value: Assumed source size 0.7'', T=200 K and propyl cyanide linewidth; derived column-density upper limit with partition function corrections

evidence.quote: Assuming a source size of 0.7$\ensuremath{''}$, a temperature of 200 K, and the same linewidth as for *n-*C$_3$H$_7$CN, we derive an upper limit

assumptions.value: Temperature scaling r^-0.83; H2 column inversely proportional to radius

evidence.quote: With a temperature scaling as r$^{-0.83}$ (cite: Rolffs11)
coupled gas-phase, grain-surface, and ice-mantle chemical kinetics model *MAGICKAL*

results_numeric.quantity: Upper limit N(n-C4H9CN) in Sgr B2(N2)

evidence.quote: we derive an upper limit to the column density of *n-*C$_4$H$_9$CN of $1.2 \times 10^{17}$ cm$^{-2}$
The resulting upper limit on the abundance ratio \[*n-*C$_4$H$_9$CN\] / \[*n-*C$_3$H$_7$CN\] = 0.59

results_numeric.quantity: Model i/n propyl cyanide, medium warm-up low EA

findings_qualitative.value: sec-butyl cyanide is predicted to be the dominant butyl cyanide form; tert form is least abundant

evidence.quote: The *sec* form of butyl cyanide is expected to be the most abundant

claims.hypothesis: Updated network with CN addition reproduces observed i:n propyl cyanide ratio
claims.experiment: MAGICKAL models with fast/medium/slow warm-up and low/high CN barriers
claims.result: Model i/n spans 0.17 to 3.0 versus observed 0.40
claims.finding: Observed ratio reproduced, best for medium to fast warm-up

evidence.quote: is well reproduced by the chemical models, with medium to fast warm-up timescales producing the best agreement.

claims.hypothesis: n-butyl cyanide is detectable in EMoCA data
claims.experiment: Searched EMoCA spectrum of Sgr B2(N2)
claims.result: Non-detection; abundance ratio to n-propyl cyanide <0.59
claims.finding: Upper limit consistent with model range 0.1–1

evidence.quote: is consistent with the predictions of our chemical models (i.e. 0.1–1)

limitations_admitted.value: Cosmic-ray ionization rate poorly constrained; full sensitivity study left for future

evidence.quote: the cosmic-ray ionization rate for Sgr B2(N2) is poorly constrained by observations

referee_caveats_inferred: Model results depend on assumed CN-addition barriers
No fit of models to observations beyond ratio comparison
